thread_pair_example: block b, one warp (ncols = 1, f16 V: nthreads_V = 128 / cpy_nb = 8 with cpy_nb = ggml_cuda_get_max_cpy_bytes() (L71, L88; common.cuh L399-409 returns 16 for CUDA __CUDA_ARCH__ >= Volta, so nthreads_V = 8 for f16 V on sm_89), V_cols_per_iter = 4): in iteration n lane 8 reads KQ slot k0 + 1 (k0 = 0, threadIdx.x/8 = 1) at L359; in iteration n+1 lane 1 writes slot 1 at L303. The only warp sync in the loop is ggml_cuda_syncwarp() (= __syncwarp(), common.cuh L127-131) at L320, which orders the L303 store before the L359 loads (RAW) but nothing orders the L359 loads of iteration n before the L303 stores of iteration n+1: the loop body ends at L377 with no sync. Between them each lane executes full-mask __shfl_xor_sync in warp_reduce_sum (L274) and at L296.
class_reason: Both accesses are plain (non-volatile, non-atomic) accesses to the shared float array KQ (verify.strong_accesses: none) by different lanes of one warp; the loop-carried WAR (read in iteration n, write in iteration n+1) has no happens-before edge unless a full-mask shfl.sync counts as an ordering point (PTX: it is not a memory-ordering operation, per the record). Plain vs plain unordered = DR under D20. Formal ITS race: in practice the next iteration's shuffles force all lanes to have issued their loads.
buggy_expected: the pair (L359 load by lane 8, iteration n) x (L303 store by lane 1, iteration n+1) on KQ is reported as DR (WAR, shared, intra-warp, loop-carried); the RAW L303 -> L359 within the iteration is ordered by the __syncwarp at L320 and must not be reported

open_questions: Discrepancy with the record: verify.accesses names L330 (f16 path) / L359 (f32 path) as the read. At 1b70350 L330 is under `#ifdef V_DOT2_F32_F16_AVAILABLE`, which common.cuh L760-762 defines only for GGML_USE_HIP (RDNA2/3/4, gfx906, CDNA); for CUDA (sm_89) the `#else` branch is compiled, so the load is L359 and KQ is float (L129), not half (L126). The oracle therefore lists L359 as the read and L330 only under other_conflicting_accesses. Everything else (store L303, __syncwarp L320, loop L254-377 with no sync at its end) is as stated.

The thread-pair arithmetic (lane 8 reads slot 1, lane 1 writes slot 1) assumes nthreads_V = 8, i.e. type_V f16 and ggml_cuda_get_max_cpy_bytes() = 16; cpy_nb = 16 on sm_89 (common.cuh L399-409), so nthreads_V = 128/16 = 8 for f16 V.

Per the record, a detector that models __shfl_xor_sync as a convergence/ordering point (not a memory barrier) would still flag it; one that treats full-mask shfl.sync as a barrier would not. The same shfl-only argument was rejected by maintainers for another kernel (llamacpp-2, mmid).
Evidence for the race at runtime is unverified: the claimed racecheck hazards come from an unmerged AI-assisted PR (28358) without logs.
Driver condition from the record: vec kernel needs kv a multiple of 256 (kv = 512 or 1024), nb = 1, nr3 == 1 and f16 K/V on sm89; host dispatch not re-verified here.
